taskDescription: Arrange this simplified pathway of dietary protein digestion and absorption in order, from the stomach to the enterocyte.
paragraphs: Gastric acid denatures dietary protein and converts pepsinogen to the active endopeptidase pepsin.
Enteropeptidase on the duodenal brush border converts pancreatic trypsinogen to active trypsin.
Trypsin activates the remaining pancreatic zymogens: chymotrypsinogen, proelastase and procarboxypeptidases.
Activated pancreatic endopeptidases cleave internal peptide bonds, producing oligopeptides in the intestinal lumen.
Brush-border aminopeptidases and dipeptidases release free amino acids and small peptides.
Free amino acids enter enterocytes through group-specific carriers, many sodium-dependent; di- and tripeptides enter via the proton-coupled transporter PepT1.

overallFeedback.feedback: This sequence summarises activation and uptake: acid and pepsin begin digestion in the stomach, enteropeptidase triggers the pancreatic zymogen cascade in the duodenum, and endopeptidase and exopeptidase actions (which overlap in practice) reduce proteins to fragments absorbed by sodium-dependent carriers and PepT1.
